rows.en: The expression on our face, the gestures we make and even proximity or way we sit, are some of the ways we send powerful messages about how we feel, or what we mean.

rows.en: Other facial actions, such as biting your lip, which indicates that you are deep in thinking, or are uncertain about something; compressing the lips, which show that you are making decisions; and a visible clenching of the teeth, to show that you are angry, are all powerful conveyers of meaning, too.

抿紧嘴唇表示你在作决定；
明显地咬紧牙齿，则表示你很生气。这些动作也都能有力地传达意义。

rows.en: And standing close to someone may be quite appropriate in some situations such as an informal party, but completely out of place in other situations, such as a meeting with a superior.
zh: 站得离别人很近，在非正式聚会等场合可能很合适，

rows.en: These features, together with linguistic features of language, like grammar, or vocabulary, are all part of the way we communicate with each other in face to face encounters.
zh: 这些特征，与语法、词汇等语言特征一起，
都构成了面对面交流方式的一部分。

rows.en: In our next lecture, we’ll watch some video material, and see how people actually use paralinguistic means in communication to express their intention or desire or mood.

了解人们在交流中如何实际运用副语言手段，来表达意图、愿望或情绪。

rows.en: Well, at one time the US was called a melting pot, you know, which means that people of many different religions, cultures, and races could shed their traditional cultural identities and blend into one homogeneous nation.

rows.en: However, it’s possible that people from different cultures have different assumptions about the world, regarding such important and basic ideas as time, personal space.
zh: 然而，来自不同文化的人，对于世界可能有不同的基本认识，
其中就涉及时间、私人空间等重要而基础的观念。

rows.en: And Edward Hall is an anthropologist who spent a large part of his life studying American Indians, their culture, their language, but he was different from a lot of other anthropologists who just study one culture.
zh: 爱德华·霍尔是一位人类学家，他一生中的很大一部分时间都在研究美洲印第安人及其文化和语言，
但他与许多只研究单一文化的人类学家不同。

rows.en: First in terms of personal space, generally speaking, in a high-context culture, because there’s greater dependency on group thinking, people lean towards heavier sensory involvement or closeness to people.
zh: 首先来看私人空间。一般来说，在高语境文化中，
由于人们更依赖群体思维，他们倾向于更多的感官接触，或与他人保持更近的距离。

rows.en: Because remember what I said, the definition of a high-context culture is that more attention is paid to the context of the message than to the message itself, and part of the context is body language.
zh: 因为，请记住我刚才说过的定义：高语境文化更关注信息的语境，而不是信息本身；
身体语言也是语境的一部分。

rows.en: A low-context culture is one in which the message, the event or the action is a separate entity, having meaning unto itself, regardless of the surroundings or the context.
zh: 在低语境文化中，信息、事件或行为是独立的实体，
自身就具有意义，不依赖周围的情境或语境。

rows.en: There’s more emphasis on individuality, so the concept of privacy is very very important, whereas before as I said, in a high-context culture they might not even be concerned with privacy or personal space.
zh: 这里更强调个体性，所以隐私的观念非常、非常重要；
而正如我前面所说，在高语境文化中，人们可能甚至不太在意隐私或私人空间。

rows.en: There’s a respect and a desire for privacy, and you also see that people might pay less attention to body language because as I said the message is, the message is everything.
zh: 人们尊重并且渴望拥有隐私；
你也会发现，他们可能不太关注身体语言，因为正如我所说，信息才是……信息才是一切。

rows.en: People in a low-context culture will be much more upset with lateness because they feel that everyone should follow the same time; there shouldn’t be all this flexibility with time and they expect punctuality.

rows.en: Observations in research on the other hand are made under precisely defined conditions, that is, in a systematic and objective manner, and with careful record keeping.
zh: 而研究中的观察是在明确规定的条件下开展的，

rows.en: Then how are we going to conduct observations in our research studies, and what do we need to do in order to make a scientific and objective observation?
zh: 那么，在研究中应该如何进行观察？
要做到科学、客观，我们又需要做些什么？

rows.en: Now, as you remember, the primary goal of observation is to describe behaviour, but it is in reality impossible to observe and describe all of a person’s behaviour.
zh: 大家还记得，观察的首要目标是描述行为，
但实际上，我们不可能观察并描述一个人的所有行为。

rows.en: By sampling as many different situations as possible researchers can reduce the chance that their observation results will be peculiar to a certain set of circumstances and conditions.
zh: 尽可能对多种情境取样，
能够降低观察结果只适用于某组特定情形和条件的可能性。

rows.en: For example, children do not always behave the same way with one parent as they do with the other parent, and animals do not behave the same way in zoos as they do in the wild.
zh: 例如，孩子面对父母中的一方时，表现不一定与面对另一方时相同；
动物在动物园里的行为，也和在野外不同。

rows.en: Having discussed ways to sample behaviour in research, we are now moving onto another issue, that is, what researchers should do to record behaviour as it occurs, that is whether researchers are active or passive in recording behaviour.
zh: 讨论完研究中如何进行行为取样后，我们接下来转向另一个问题：
研究人员应如何实时记录行为，也就是他们在记录时是主动介入还是被动观察。

rows.en: In participant observation, observers, that is researchers, play a dual role: They observe people’s behaviour and they participate actively in the situation they are observing.
zh: 在参与式观察中，观察者，也就是研究人员，承担双重角色：
既观察人们的行为，也积极参与所观察的情境。

rows.en: If individuals who are being observed know that the observer is present to collect information about their behaviour, this is undisguised participant observation.
zh: 如果被观察者知道，观察者在场是为了收集他们的行为信息，
这就属于公开的参与式观察。

rows.en: When an observer controls one or more conditions in a natural setting in order to determine their effect on behaviour, this procedure is called field experiment.
zh: 观察者在自然环境中控制一个或多个条件，以确定这些条件对行为的影响，
这种研究程序就叫实地实验。

rows.en: Observation without intervention is also called naturalistic observation because its main purpose is to describe behaviour as it normally occurs, that is, in a natural setting, without any attempt by the observer to intervene.
zh: 无干预观察也叫自然观察，因为它主要用于描述行为自然发生时的样子，
也就是在自然环境中观察，而观察者不作任何干预。

rows.en: In order to define active learning, I will look at the differences between active learning and passive learning by examining six characteristics of active learners and contrasting them with those of passive learners.
zh: 为了给主动学习下定义，我会考察主动学习和被动学习的区别，
方法是考察主动学习者的六个特点，并将它们与被动学习者的特点作比较。

rows.en: However, I am sure that some of you have been in a situation, probably more than once, where you read — quote and unquote — an assignment, closed the text and thought “what the world was that about?”
zh: 不过，我确信你们中有些人可能不止一次遇到过这种情况：
所谓“读过了”布置的阅读材料，合上书，却在想：“刚才那到底讲了些什么？”

rows.en: For instance, you may make connections between the new information and what you already know, identify concepts that you may not understand very well or evaluate the importance of what you are reading.
zh: 例如，你可以把新信息与已有知识联系起来，
找出自己可能不太理解的概念，或者评估所读内容的重要性。

rows.en: In contrast, passive learners may read the text and listen to lectures and even understand most of what is read and heard, but they do not take that crucial next step of actually thinking about it.
zh: 相比之下，被动学习者可能也读文章、听讲座，甚至理解大部分读到和听到的内容，
但他们没有迈出至关重要的下一步：真正思考这些内容。

rows.en: Because active learners are constantly monitoring their understanding, they know when their comprehension breaks down, and they ask for help before they become lost.
zh: 因为主动学习者一直在检查自己的理解情况，
所以他们知道自己何时出现理解障碍，并会在完全跟不上之前求助。

rows.en: Active learners may seek assistance from their professors or peers, although passive learners may seek help at some point, it is often too little, too late.
zh: 主动学习者可能会向老师或同学求助；
被动学习者虽然也可能在某个时候求助，但往往已经为时过晚，所获帮助也不足以解决问题。

rows.en: This means that active learners raise questions on information that they read and hear, while passive learners accept both the printed page and the words of their professors as truth.
zh: 这意味着，主动学习者会对读到和听到的信息提出问题，
而被动学习者则把书面材料和老师的话都当作真理接受。

rows.en: Active learners understand that the responsibility for learning must come from within, while passive learners often want to blame others for their lack of motivation, poor performance, time management problems and other difficulties that they might experience.
zh: 主动学习者明白，学习的责任必须由自己承担；
而被动学习者则往往想把问题归咎于别人：
自己缺乏动力、表现不佳、时间管理混乱，以及可能遇到的其他困难。

rows.en: When active learners don’t perform as well as they’d hoped, they evaluate why they didn’t do well and change those studying behaviors the next time.
zh: 当主动学习者表现没有达到预期时，
他们会分析原因，并在下一次改变相应的学习行为。

rows.en: By skill, I mean the tools to handle the studying and learning demands placed on you, like how to read with purpose, when and where to get assistance if you are having difficulty.
zh: 所谓技能，是指应对学习要求所需的方法，
例如如何有目的地阅读，以及遇到困难时应在何时、向何处求助。

rows.en: For example, you may have a friend who is knowledgeable, but not motivated in the classroom, even though he reads widely and can intelligently discuss a variety of issues, he does little school work and rarely studies.
zh: 例如，你可能有一位知识丰富、却在课堂上缺乏动力的朋友。
他虽然阅读广泛，也能有见地地讨论各种问题，却很少做功课，也很少学习。

rows.en: OK, today we’ve discussed the differences between an active learner and a passive one, and some useful study strategies that may eventually help you become an active learner.
zh: 今天，我们讨论了主动学习者和被动学习者的区别，
以及一些实用的学习策略，希望最终能帮助大家成为主动学习者。

rows.en: Then in the 1930s, a doctor named Hans Selye, S-e-l-y-e, first used this term to describe a human’s reaction to a demand placed on it, pleasant or not.
zh: 到了二十世纪三十年代，一位名叫汉斯·塞利的医生——姓氏拼作S-e-l-y-e——
首次用这个术语描述人对外界要求所作出的反应，无论这种要求令人愉快与否。

rows.en: So psychologists have found that if we develop appropriate ways to cope with stressful situations, individuals can reduce the physiological harm which is caused by stress, or which can be caused by stress.
zh: 心理学家因此发现，如果我们学会以适当的方式应对压力情境，
就能够减轻压力已经造成或可能造成的生理伤害。

rows.en: We all have different types of stress signals, but individuals should monitor themselves for stress signals so that they can focus on minimizing or acknowledging the stress before it gets out of control.
zh: 每个人的压力信号各不相同，但我们都应该留意自身的这些信号，
以便在压力失控之前，着手减轻它，或者正视它的存在。

rows.en: You can consider ways to protect yourself when you start seeing these signs coming on, so you might decide to withdraw from a stressful situation or reward yourself with equal amounts of low stress activity time.
zh: 开始察觉这些迹象时，就可以考虑如何保护自己。
比如，选择暂时离开压力情境，或者奖励自己等量时间，去参加压力较小的活动。

rows.en: And this seems quite apparent because exercise can provide a stress-free environment away from your usual stressors, and it keeps your body busy and preoccupied with non-stressful things.
zh: 这似乎很容易理解：锻炼能提供一个远离日常压力源的无压力环境，
还能让身体忙起来，专注于不会造成压力的事情。

rows.en: You can make plans and act when it’s appropriate, but when it’s not appropriate or when it’s impossible, the only way is to learn to accept that some things are unchangeable, and out of your hands.
zh: 时机合适时，可以制订计划并行动；而时机不合适，或者根本无法行动时，
唯一的办法就是学会接受：有些事是改变不了、也不由你掌控的。

rows.en: But if you say to yourself: today I’m going to the library and gather resources; tomorrow I’m going to read three articles, and so on, you will have broken this one large task, that’s writing a term paper, down into many smaller and more manageable tasks.
zh: 但如果你告诉自己：今天去图书馆找资料，明天读三篇文章，以此类推，
那么，你就把写学期论文这一项大任务，分解成了许多更小、更容易完成的任务。

rows.en: Now, at the university, you, as students, are often called on to perform many types of listening tasks: listening in a group discussion, listening to a teacher on a one-to-one basis, and listening to academic lectures.
zh: 在大学里，作为学生，你们经常需要完成各种听力任务：
听小组讨论、与老师一对一交谈，以及听学术讲座。

rows.en: So the meaning is not in the word alone, rather it is in the person who uses it or responds to it so that the second thing that a listener must do— add information that the lecturer assumes that they share.
zh: 因此，意义并不只存在于词语本身，也存在于使用这些词语、或对其作出回应的人身上。所以，听众要做的第二件事，
就是补充讲课人假定双方都知道的信息。

rows.en: And then all of a sudden, you'll remember “Oh, I’ve got to listen.” By being able to predict during the lecture, you can just keep listening to the lecture and not lose the idea of what’s going on.
zh: 随后，你会突然想起来：“哦，我得认真听。”如果你能在听讲时进行预测，
就能继续跟上讲座，而不会失去对当前内容的理解。

rows.en: Now when you listen you need time to think about the information, relate it to old ideas, take notes, and if you’re only keeping up with what I’m saying or what the lecturer’s saying, you have no time to do that.
zh: 听讲时，你需要时间来思考信息、把它与已有的想法联系起来，以及记笔记；
如果你只是勉强跟上我或讲课人的讲话，就没有时间做这些事了。

rows.en: And I’ll bet a lot of you are having that problem right now because it’s so hard just to follow everything I’m saying, that you don’t have time to note down ideas.
zh: 我敢说，你们中很多人现在就有这个问题：光是跟上我说的全部内容，就已经很费力了，
因而没有时间记下要点。

rows.en: Now let’s come to the last thing a listener must do: the listener must evaluate, as he or she is listening, decide what’s important, what’s not, decide how something relates to something else.
zh: 现在来看听众必须做的最后一件事：边听边评价，
判断什么重要、什么不重要，以及某件事与另一件事之间有什么联系。

rows.en: From what I’ve said so far, you can see there’s a lot involved in listening to lectures: language awareness, adding information, making predictions and evaluations.
zh: 从刚才的内容可以看出，听讲座涉及很多事情：
语言意识、补充信息、进行预测和作出评价。

rows.en: Because they have been giving a message that there are barriers there, and we’ve seen it today, there are reports already that Cambridge has been finding state school pupils ringing up and saying that they are not going to bother to apply now.
zh: 因为他们一直在传递“有障碍挡在那里”的信息。我们今天就看到了这一点：

rows.en: Now one of the ways they want to do it is to give the schools the opportunity to run themselves more completely than they are doing at the moment, to give schools more powers, exactly the same as you.

rows.en: The present government talks about freedom for schools, it talks about getting money into schools, but if you look in the detail of what they are proposing, the reality is very different.
zh: 现任政府在谈学校自由，也在谈把钱投入学校。
但只要仔细看看他们提出的方案，就会发现实际情况完全不同。

rows.en: So, at the moment, a certain amount of money goes to schools, a certain amount of money goes to local education authorities, are you saying that in future, no money will go to Local Education Authorities, but all of the money will go to the schools.

您的意思是，将来将不再有经费拨给地方教育主管部门，而是全部拨给学校？

rows.en: At the moment, what happens is that money goes to Local Education Authorities and they decide how much money is then going to be spent on the schools.
zh: 目前的情况是，经费先拨给地方教育主管部门，

rows.en: Money is held back at those Education Authorities, and is held back initially at Central Government as well, for them to decide how it should be spent.
zh: 有些钱被扣留在这些教育主管部门，
